source.title: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks: A Sharpness-Aware Minimization Perspective and Beyond
source.authors: Chong-Yu Fan; Jing-Han Jia; Yihua Zhang; Anil Ramakrishna; Ming-Yi Hong; Si-Jia Liu

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning attacks recover unlearned information and whether smoothness-based counter-methods reduce that recovery. It uses a different intervention from the original unlearning recipes rather than explicitly reproducing an original study.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses cited relearning and jailbreaking results, but those cited results are not recorded as rows. Hyperparameter search ranges and values selected during tuning are not rows. Loss-landscape figures and the per-token KL analysis do not directly measure recovery of the targeted behavior, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs relearning (forget-set and unrelated-data) and enhanced-GCG jailbreak attacks on NPO-, GradDiff- and RMU-unlearned models (WMDP Bio, MUSE) and reports recovery. It then proposes smoothness-based variants (SAM, RS, GP, CR, WA) that claim to resist those attacks, and compares them with TAR and RMU-LAT. Its own numbers bear on A, B, E and F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also show vanilla NPO nearly reverts to pre-unlearning performance under small relearning attacks. They present SAM as the strongest defense against relearning and jailbreaks, with no loss of unattacked UE or utility. The paper does not itself stress that robustness is incomplete; that follows from its numbers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper tests NPO, GradDiff, and RMU with SAM or other smoothness modifications, and evaluates relearning fine-tuning attacks. It does not reproduce the original methods as a standalone study of recovery, and does not test quantization or activation-direction ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning sample count and epoch count change UE; relearning dataset changes the tested setting; SAM perturbation radius ρ affects outcomes, with 0.001 providing limited improvement and 0.1 disrupting forgetting; the number of parameters perturbed in RMU changes robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-token KL divergence under jailbreak is small at the first few tokens for NPO and larger for the smooth variants. The authors call this 'shallow unlearning alignment'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning is concentrated beyond the first output tokens, leaving early tokens close to the original model.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss landscapes on the forget set are sharp around NPO-unlearned weights and flatter with smoothing; the authors link flatness to relearning robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearned minima are sharp in weight space, enabling fast relearning.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 2025
record.problems: The paper does not compare attacks against a never-trained model. Several results are provided only in figures without exact values. The reported attack results are averaged over 5 independent random trials, but no uncertainty estimates are stated in the supplied text. Some comparisons use UE and MUSE memorization metrics that are not directly expressed as recovery relative to a never-trained model.
record.rows_left_out: The full per-method WMDP table includes additional attack-setting cells for NPO+RS, NPO+CR, NPO+GP, and NPO+WA beyond the selected 60-sample and 3-epoch comparisons; omitted cells are in Table 2. The paper also reports the full NPO/GradDiff/RMU and SAM comparisons in Table A1, additional LLaMA-3 8B comparisons in Table 1, and MUSE ρ ablation results in Table A3. The selected rows prioritize vanilla versus SAM recovery, the unrelated-dataset attacks, MUSE recovery, and jailbreaking outcomes.

untested.parts: No comparison with a never-trained model. Near-chance accuracy is shown only implicitly (UE 0.74 ≈ 26% accuracy on 4-choice items).
Loosely related relearning data is not tested; only forget-set subsets and unrelated datasets are.
Not tested: no activation ablation and no blocking-versus-deletion analysis.
Only enhanced-GCG prefixes are tested. Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information are not.
The counter-methods are not tested against quantization, activation ablation or non-GCG prompting.

missing.what: LLaMA-3 8B: NPO 0.73→0.41, TAR 0.74→0.70, RMU-LAT 0.70→0.44, NPO+SAM 0.74→0.70 (60 samples, 1 epoch)
GradDiff, GradDiff+SAM, RMU and RMU+SAM UE under N=20/40/60 and M=1/2/3 (e.g., RMU 0.66→0.36)
RMU+SAM by perturbed-layer count under 20 samples, 3 epochs (0.36, 0.38, 0.41)
NPO+CR, NPO+GP and NPO+WA UE under GCG; these appear to drop (bar labels about 0.63, 0.53, 0.45)
Origin WMDP UE 0.35, needed as the full-recovery reference
MUSE pre-attack News KnowMem Df (NPO 43.93, SAM 42.26) and origin values
ρ ablation: ρ=0.001 gives VerbMem 70.9 after attack (worse than NPO); ρ=0.1 hurts utility (23.91)

record.verdict_notes: Fixes against the record: r9 duplicates r4. r27 and r28 carry Books KnowMem values in place of News values. r14's baseline is off by 0.01. F was wrongly attached to vanilla-NPO rows and A to counter-method rows. Figure-only values (Figs. 4, 6a) were read from text-extracted bar labels, so the bar-to-method mapping is uncertain. MUSE relearn sample counts are inconsistent (text says 75/100/125; Fig. 5 caption says 200–600) and not stated for Table A2.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not state that targeted accuracy is near chance, and it does not compare attack recovery against a model that never learned the knowledge. It reports unlearning effectiveness and utility metrics, then measures their change after attacks.
The relearning attacks use forget-set examples or examples from the named unrelated datasets; the paper does not test all possible loosely related data or every subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation is performed, and the paper does not test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
Tests enhanced-GCG adversarial prefixes, not prompt rephrasing generally, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests SAM and other smoothness-based methods against the paper's fine-tuning relearning attacks and enhanced-GCG jailbreaking, not against quantization or internal activation-direction ablation.
